title: Hybrid entitlement microbundle & SLA hedging playbook
author: Priya Rao
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a repeatable commercial and product approach for offering short-duration 'microbundle' trials and an SLA-hedging mechanism for hybrid consumption customers (hosted + dedicated). The intent is to accelerate developer adoption, limit revenue leakage, and provide predictable economics during onboarding and early growth while preserving predictable capacity guarantees.

Goals

- Reduce friction for new tenants to test production traffic without committing to full reserved capacity.
- Maintain clear SLOs and a hedging policy so Redwood can minimize risk from microburst-heavy customers.
- Produce a commercial template (pricing + credits + SLA concessions) that sales and CSMs can use consistently.

Scope

In-scope:
- Short-term microbundle (1–30 day) trial offerings for new or expanding tenants.
- SLA hedging policy when customers exceed microbundle allocations via burst credits and automated throttles.
- Billing hooks and telemetry required to reconcile microbundle usage to long-term packages.

Out-of-scope:
- Permanent reserved-capacity contract changes; those are handled by the Dedicated commercial team.
- Non-consumption addons (e.g., premium support upgrades) which follow normal pricing flows.

Key definitions

- Microbundle: A time-limited package of capacity credits (token or session credits) sold or granted as a trial to evaluate production impact. Typical durations: 7, 14, 30 days.
- Hedging window: A short period (48–168 hours) after a microbundle allotment is exhausted during which automatic soft-fallback rules and credits apply to avoid abrupt failures.
- SLA hedge credit: A negotiated credit returned to the customer when Redwood fails to meet agreed throughput/latency SLOs while serving within the aspired capacity profile.

Principles and guardrails

1) Predictable economics: Each microbundle must have a defined unit price and an 'overage path' that prevents unlimited consumption charges.
2) Safety-first: If a customer’s traffic profile risks degrading multi-tenant pools, automated throttles and fallback variants must engage before capacity commitments are violated.
3) Clear observability: Owners and customers must be able to see projected spend, current consumption, and remaining microbundle credits in the Console and via API.
4) Commercial simplicity: Sales and CSM playbooks should provide at most three microbundle templates to reduce negotiation friction.

Commercial templates (recommended)

- Starter: 7 days, 10k token-equivalent credits, no SLA, low-touch onboarding (self-serve).
- Evaluation: 14 days, 100k token-equivalent credits, hedging window of 72h, limited SLA-hedge credit (5% of spend) if platform SLOs breached.
- Proof-of-Value (POV): 30 days, 500k token-equivalent credits, hedging window 168h, SLA-hedge credit up to 15% of spend plus 1:1 migration credit toward first reserved commit.

Pricing and billing flow (technical summary)

1. Purchase/grant: Microbundle issued as allocation_id in billing ledger.
2. Consumption: Real-time meter decrements allocation; Console shows remaining credits.
3. Exhaustion: On allocation exhaustion, hedging window starts (if included); automated fallback policies engage.
4. Post-window reconciliation: If overage occurred during hedging and SLO breach verified, SLA hedge credit computed and applied.

Sample pricing config (YAML format for config service)

---
microbundle_template_id: pov-30
name: "POV 30-day"
duration_days: 30
credits_tokens: 500000
hedging_window_hours: 168
sla_hedge_pct: 0.15
overage_path: "soft_fallback_then_billing"
---

Platform and API changes required

- Billing service: support allocation_id lifecycle, hedging_window tracking, and SLA credit issuance. Owner: finance-billing.
- Runtime routing: integrate a "microbundle-identifier" token in routing metadata for priority selection and traceability. Owner: serving-runtime.
- Console: add microbundle usage card and projected exhaustion alerts (owner: console/observability).
- Telemetry: expose events: MICROBUNDLE_ALLOCATED, MICROBUNDLE_EXHAUSTED, HEDGING_WINDOW_START, HEDGING_SLO_BREACH_DETECTED. Owner: eng-platform/telemetry.

Operational playbook (onboarding and incident flows)

Pre-onboarding checklist (CSM/Sales)
1. Confirm chosen microbundle template with customer and document expected traffic profile.
2. Record allocation_id and attach to customer tenant in billing.
3. Create a short runbook with expected SLOs, emergency contact, and fallback preferences.

During microbundle (automated + manual)
- Automated: System sends daily digest + real-time low-credit (10%) and exhausted alerts. If runtime detects burst risk, apply throttles and variant fallback.
- Manual: CSM will proactively reach out at 50% usage with suggestions for model fidelity, batching, or upgrade paths.

Hedging window incident steps (if exhaustion triggers hedging)
1. SYSTEM: Start hedging window; automatically route to fallback variant that preserves latency SLO (if available).
2. TELEMETRY: Begin high-fidelity capture for 72–168h depending on template.
3. SRE/CSM: If SLOs breached, create a postmortem and flag for SLA credit calculation.
4. FINANCE: Calculate SLA hedge credit (formula below) and apply to account ledger.

SLA credit calculation (formula)

- baseline_spend = sum(billed tokens consumed during hedging_window)
- credit = baseline_spend * sla_hedge_pct * quality_multiplier
- quality_multiplier = 1.0 by default, 0.5 if customer triggered multiple non-runtime errors (see exclusions)

Example: baseline_spend $12,000, sla_hedge_pct 0.15 -> credit $1,800 (subject to review).

Telemetry and acceptance criteria

Core metrics to track during a microbundle:
- consumption_rate (tokens/min) and tail percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
- average latency and 99th percentile latency per route
- % of requests served by fallback variants
- microbundle exhaustion lead time (time between expected exhaustion and actual)
- conversion rate to paid commitment within 30 days of expiry

Success criteria for POV template pilot (90 days):
- >25% conversion to paid reserved or hybrid commitments
- median time-to-first-failure < 1 minute when overload protection triggers (indicating fast protection)
- Console adoption: >70% of POV customers use Console alerts at least once

Migration and UX requirements

- Console must display an upgrade CTA when remaining credits < 20% with pre-filled recommended packages.
- API must return allocation metadata on DescribeTenant endpoints: { allocation_id, template_id, expires_at, remaining_credits }.
- If customer accepts a reserved commit during microbundle, remaining credits should be auto-converted to migration credits per template policy.

Security and compliance notes

- Microbundle telemetry must be tagged and stored under the tenant's existing retention policy; do not extend retention by default.
- SLA hedging calculations must be auditable; store calculation inputs in finance audit logs for 7 years.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Abuse of microbundles by high-volume spammers.
  Mitigation: Require low-friction verification for POV templates (email + rate-limit onboarding) and enforce per-tenant burst caps.
- Risk: Platform cost overruns during hedging windows.
  Mitigation: Cap SLA credit exposure per template and require Sales approval for exceptional hedges.
- Risk: Customer confusion about fallback behavior.
  Mitigation: In-product messaging and explicit consent during purchase; default to conservative fallback policies.

Roadmap and milestones (next 6 months)

Month 0–1: Finalize commercial templates, policy doc, and pricing config.
Month 1–3: Implement billing allocation lifecycle and Console UI cards.
Month 2–4: Runtime routing metadata & telemetry events. Pilot with 10 customers in controlled POV cohort.
Month 4–6: Iterate on hedging credit formula, integrate Sales/CS workflows, and broaden to general availability.

Ownership and stakeholders

- Product (owner): Priya Rao — primary playbook author and GTM coordinator.
- Eng: Serving-runtime (owner: Arjun Mehta), Billing (owner: Finance-Billing), Console (owner: Console UX).
- GTM: Sales lead (Evan Thompson), CSM (Sofia Martinez).
- Finance: Credit reconciliation and audit owner.

Title: "POV credits remaining"
Body: "You have 120k tokens remaining in your 30-day POV. Upgrade to a reserved commit to convert unused credits into migration credits and unlock improved latency SLAs."
